text.p: Earthlink Network Inc said it was retracting an erroneous statement in its 10-Q filing with the Securities and Exchange Commission which said its current cash would not be sufficient to meet its operating expenses through the end of its fiscal year.

Earthlink said it was optimistic that financing alternatives are available to meet liquidity requirements and will amend its 10-Q Thursday to correct the public record after several news reports carried the earlier statement.
"We do have enough cash to meet our operating expenses through this year," Garry Betty, chief executive officer, told Reuters.
The Internet service provider said it plans to raise additional cash from existing investors, institutional investors, strategic partners or by taking on additional debt.
At June 30, the company said it held cash and cash equivalents of $6.2 million versus a mere $1.2 million at the same time one year ago.
"In order to proceed with ready access to capital, we're taking the steps now to secure additional sources of financing," Betty said.

"We want to have cash reserves in order to fund rapid expansions or acquisitions. We're doing the smart thing by making sure we get the financing and we expect to secure financing arrangements totaling about $10 million before the end of the year," he said.
